title: Compatibility bridge: maintain tokenizer/KV/context parity across model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The smart routing subsystem needs a reliable compatibility map between model variants so the router can fallback safely without corrupting chat state or producing tokenization regressions. Recent incidents showed subtle tokenizer/token count mismatches and KV cache layout differences when routing between primary and fallback variants, causing broken tool calls and truncated contexts.

Goal: Establish and operate a 'compatibility bridge' that documents and enforces tokenizer, context length, and tooling parity across variants. Provide automated checks, metadata flags, and router safeguards so fallback is lossless for common workloads.

Scope: Audit current hosted and dedicated variants that are eligible for smart routing fallbacks; publish a compatibility matrix; implement CI/telemetry gating for new variant onboarding and for periodic parity sweeps; add router checks and graceful fallback behavior when parity is uncertain.

Out of scope: Model quality parity (semantic/regression testing outside tokenizer/context/tooling), on‑prem private customer variant onboarding workflows (handled by private deployment backlog).
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility matrix document exists listing tokenizer version, tokenizer config (special tokens, byte fallback), canonical token counts on canonical prompts, declared max context window, KV cache layout tag, and tooling hooks for each variant.
CI job added that runs tokenizer parity tests on every model variant PR and fails if tokenization differs for the canonical test corpus beyond an agreed tolerance.
Smart router consults the matrix at routing time and rejects fallbacks to variants marked 'incompatible' for a request's toolchain/context requirements, logging a clear reason.
Telemetry emits a parity_score metric per-variant and an alert when parity_score degrades by >5% week-over-week for any critical route.
Runbook documented for remediation steps when parity failures are detected (label variant, create remediation ticket, temporary routing block).
tasks: Perform audit of hosted/dedicated variants and capture tokenizer binary/version, tokenizer-config.json, declared context window, kv-cache-layout tag for each variant.
Create a canonical prompt set (200 prompts) that covers unicode, emojis, multilingual, code snippets, tool call examples, and edge BOS/EOS usages.
Build tokenizer parity CI using a lightweight runner that tokenizes canonical prompts with old/new variant tokenizers and reports differences (counts + token-id diffs summary).
Add a model metadata field 'compat_bridge_status' with values: compatible|incompatible|unknown and a kv_cache_layout tag to model registry entries.
Implement router pre-check: consult compat_bridge_status and kv_cache_layout before issuing fallback; if unknown, prefer same-variant family fallback or fallback to stateless low-latency model.
Instrument telemetry: parity_score, tokenizer_mismatch_rate, kv_layout_mismatch_count; wire alerts to PagerDuty when mismatch_count > 3 in 1h for production routes.
Author runbook and on-call playbook for parity incidents (link included in comments).
Schedule monthly parity sweep job and build a dashboard in Console listing parity trends and top mismatching prompts.
notes: 2025-02-15: Initial inventory completed. Found 18 variants in scope across hosted/dedicated; 4 have no kv_cache_layout tag and 6 use older tokenizer binaries (v0.9.x). — Aisha

2025-02-20: Built canonical prompt set; included 40 edge cases around emoji modifiers and mixed RTL/LTR scripts. Early token counts show variance between xformer-compat variants and newer fused-tokenizer builds. — Mateo

2025-02-24: Prototype CI job added on feature branch; it runs tokenization diffs and produces a condensed diff artifact. Failing causes are primarily special-token mapping (tool call delimiter tokens) and byte-fallback differences. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721 — (review requested by Priya)

2025-02-26: Priya Nair review: asked for clearer failure thresholds (we should allow up to 1 token count difference for non-tooling prompts but zero tolerance when tool delimiters differ). Also requested metric labels include route_id and tenant_id. Action: update CI thresholds and telemetry labels. — Priya Nair

2025-03-01: Mateo implemented metadata field 'compat_bridge_status' on model registry; default set to 'unknown' until CI completes. Added simple router check that blocks fallback to 'incompatible' variants; rollback path routes to same-family variant. Deployed to staging. — Mateo

2025-03-03: Smoke test on staging with canary route; detected a mismatch on a Spanish prompts cohort caused by tokenizer normalization differences. Filed ENG-261540 for remediation on the tokenizer build. Temporarily marked offending variant as 'incompatible' to prevent production fallback. — Aisha
comments: Priya Nair (2025-02-25): We need a documented tolerance table: tool-call-critical vs conversational. Also add a test for tool payload boundary tokens (|CALL_START| / |CALL_END|).
Jonas Berg (PM) (2025-02-27): Good approach. Make sure the console dashboard surfaces which tenants might have degraded fallback options so Support can proactively reach out.
Infra (2025-02-28): CI runner needs a lightweight container image with both tokenizer artifacts; recommend using s3 cache for tokenizer binaries to speed runs. Added as infra task.
